findings.text: Every fixture file this case writes names a root under tmp_path that was never created (`"root": str(tmp_path / f"gone-{index}" / "docs")`), so all of them are removed by _prune_snapshots' "its tree is gone" branch. Deleting the `index >= _SNAPSHOT_KEEP_PER_PROJECT` branch from reckon/roadmap_snapshot.py leaves `assert len(remaining) <= kept` (:990) green, so the keep-count bound the case is named for has no assertion that fails when it is removed. The dead-tree prune (a sibling finding from the review at 280bf2cf5) is genuinely guarded; this half of the same repair is not.

The checkpoint attributes the node's one added failing id (tests/test_plan_read_warns_unparsed.py::test_every_live_plan_under_docs_plans_reads_without_the_warning, 303.44 s against a 300 s bound at s50-added-id-rerun.log:9) to this worktree's filesystem under load, citing "a scratch copy of this revision's content passes the same case in 42 s" and per-plan read timings of 14.5 s against 14.7 s. The only scratch arm on disk is s50-added-id-base-arm.log, whose tree is /tmp/reckon-crew-scratch/.../tree280 at revision 280bf2cf5 — the reviewed base, not this head — and no log under the run directory records either the head scratch arm or the 14.5/14.7 s measurement. The attribution is plausible and the id is correctly reported as added rather than hidden, but the arm that would settle it was not run at the head, so a coordinator cannot check the claim from the evidence.

baseline_suite.failure_ids reads ["the base log lists them"], which is prose rather than the pytest node-id form the reviewed done_when requires of both arms. The 38 ids are recoverable only by parsing /home/ITER/mcintos/.cache/reckon-raid/s50-base-04c10e00c.log, which I did: base has 38 ids, s50-head-population.log has 39, the set difference is exactly the one id recorded in added_failure_ids, and no id present at base is absent at head. The record's numbers are right; the field's shape is what the gate refuses, so the ids that the delta rests on are not in the record that states the delta.

The landed fragment says the key stats its plan directories "through the discovery index's own covered_dir_identity, which reuses the observation an open discovery pass has already made". Both key builds on the read path — reckon/mcp.py:1802 (before) and :1860 (settled) — run outside any discovery scope; reckon/metadata_index.discovery_file_scope() is entered only at reckon/mcp.py:1850 around _roadmap_scoped and exited before the second build. So on a cold read the three plan directories are stat'd twice (six stats), and on a warm read three times once, with no reused observation. The source docstring (reckon/roadmap_snapshot.py:_covered_directory_shape) correctly conditions the claim on "while one is in force"; the fragment drops the condition and states a saving that this call path does not get.
